title: cleanup silently SKIPS pauser restoration on the JSON catch-path: live staker unpaused but left with the deployer EOA as pauser; post-assert passes vacuously
function: run (origPauser/tempPauser try/catch read + gated setPauser restore)
description: cleanup reads origPauser/tempPauser from ys-swap-deployments.json via try/catch (~132-143). On the CATCH path (JSON missing the keys — e.g. a deploy run before the hardening, or a regenerated/partial JSON), origPauserRecorded stays false and the setPauser restore (~342) is gated on that flag, so it is SKIPPED with only a console WARNING. The unpause (gated on paused()) still runs and the post-asserts require !paused, so the staker is reopened — but its pauser remains the deployer EOA (set by the deploy step) rather than the original pauser contract 0x7c5A8EeF..85a3. The post-asserts only check pauser==recorded when *Recorded is true (~373-384), so they pass vacuously on the catch path and do not catch the wrong-pauser end state.
impact: After a catch-path cleanup the emergency-pause authority on the LIVE staker is left as the deployer EOA instead of the intended governance pauser contract 0x7c5A8EeF..85a3 — a silent privilege/wiring drift. No availability loss (the staker IS reopened) and no fund loss; the defect is purely the wrong pauser ADDRESS left installed on the degraded catch-path, with the post-assert passing vacuously and not catching the wrong end state. The run is reported COMPLETE with only a buried warning. Owner-fixable. Non-obvious Law-3 footgun (operator believes cleanup restored the original pauser).
attackPath: 1. cleanup runs against a JSON missing origPauser/tempPauser (deploy before hardening, or regenerated/partial JSON).
2. try/catch leaves origPauserRecorded=false; setPauser restore (~342) is gated on that flag -> SKIPPED with only a console warning.
3. unpause runs; post-assert (pauser==recorded gated on *Recorded) is vacuously true.

4. Live staker reopened but emergency-pause authority left as the deployer EOA instead of the governance pauser 0x7c5A8EeF..85a3 — silent privilege/wiring drift, run reported COMPLETE with a buried warning.
forkEvidence: subagent line-trace: catch leaves recorded*=false, setPauser gated on *Recorded -> skipped; post-assert pauser==recorded gated on *Recorded -> vacuously true. Happy-path on the fork DID restore correctly (JSON present, pauser restored to 0x7c5A8EeF..85a3), so this only bites the degraded-input (missing-keys) path.
recommendation: On the catch path, FAIL LOUDLY (revert) rather than warn-and-continue, OR re-read the pre-pause pauser from an alternate source; and make the post-assert unconditional (require pauser != deployer after restore). At minimum elevate the warning so an operator cannot miss that the pauser was not restored.
